title: Maximum Enemy Forts That Can Be Captured
statement:
The array `forts` describes a row of positions: `1` is a fort you command, `0` is an enemy fort and `-1` is an empty position.

You may make one move: send your army from a position `i` holding your fort to an empty position `j` (on either side), provided every position strictly between `i` and `j` holds an enemy fort. All the enemy forts passed on the way are captured.

Return the largest number of enemy forts a single move can capture. If no move is possible (for instance you command no fort, or there is no empty position you can reach), return `0`.
notes:
## Intuition

A move goes from a `1` to a `-1` with only `0`s in between, so the two ends are *neighbouring* non-zero positions. Checking every pair of a `1` and a `-1` works in O(n²), but it is enough to look at each pair of consecutive non-zero positions: if one is `1` and the other is `-1`, the zeros between them can all be captured.

## Approach

1. Keep `left` at the most recent non-zero position (`-1` before there is one) and `best = 0`.
2. Move `right` across the array, skipping zeros.
3. At a non-zero `right`, if `left` exists and `forts[left]` is the opposite of `forts[right]`, the gap `right - left - 1` is a valid capture; keep the larger of it and `best`.
4. Set `left = right` and continue. Return `best`.

## Example 1, step by step

`forts = [1, 0, 0, -1, 0, 0, 0, 0, 1]`.

- `right = 0`: value `1`, no `left` yet; `left = 0`.
- `right = 3`: value `-1`, `forts[0] = 1` is its opposite, gap `3 - 0 - 1 = 2`, `best = 2`; `left = 3`.
- `right = 8`: value `1`, `forts[3] = -1` is its opposite, gap `8 - 3 - 1 = 4`, `best = 4`; `left = 8`.

The answer is `4`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n): `right` visits each position once and `left` only jumps forward.
- Space: O(1).

## Pitfalls

- The army may move in either direction, so test `forts[left] === -forts[right]` rather than requiring the `1` to be on the left.
- Two `1`s or two `-1`s with zeros between them are not a valid move.
- Do not reset `left` only on `1`s: any non-zero position blocks the path, so it must become the new `left`.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `left` | index of the previous non-zero position, or `-1` |
| `right` | index currently scanned |
| `best` | most enemy forts captured by any valid move so far |

narration.2: No move found yet, so the best capture is 0.
narration.3: left will remember the last position that is not an enemy fort; -1 means none yet.
narration.4: Scan every position from left to right.
narration.5: Enemy forts only lie between endpoints, so skip them.
narration.8: A move is possible when the previous non-zero position holds the opposite value: one of your forts and one empty spot.
narration.9: Everything strictly between left and right is an enemy fort; count them and keep the maximum.
narration.11: This position blocks any path through it, so it becomes the new left end.
narration.13: Every pair of neighbouring non-zero positions was checked; return the best capture.
